Product Description
This is a men's short-sleeve printed custom ringer T-shirt made in Japan by TOYS McCOY. Produced as part of the TOYS McCOY 30th Anniversary collection, this T-shirt combines a vintage-inspired tubular jersey body with original commemorative graphic artwork created by the brand. It incorporates classic ringer T-shirt details, such as a contrast rib-knit neckband and sleeve trim, while also featuring a compact Japanese fit with a trim silhouette and relatively shorter body length. The result is a refined casual T-shirt that balances vintage character, detailed construction, and everyday wearability.

Fabric
The fabric is a heavyweight 100% cotton tubular jersey with a non-washed finish. It has a substantial hand feel with enough thickness and body to give the garment a solid presence, while still retaining the natural softness and flexibility of cotton. The surface is not overly smooth or flat; instead, it has a dry, textured character with subtle yarn irregularities, fine slub-like texture, and small nep-like variations. These natural surface qualities create visual depth and give the fabric a vintage-inspired appearance. The vertical structure of the knit is also visible, adding a slight three-dimensional texture to the material.

Tubular Jersey Body
The body is knitted on a circular knitting machine and made with a tubular construction. This means that the body is knitted in a continuous tube-like form rather than being made from separate front and back panels sewn together at the sides. Because there are no side seams, the garment has a cleaner appearance around the body and a more natural drape when worn. The absence of side seams also reduces bulk and friction at the sides, contributing to a smoother and more comfortable feel against the skin.

Non-Washed Finish
This T-shirt is supplied in a non-washed condition, meaning it has not been washed during the manufacturing process. Because of this, the fabric may feel slightly open or relaxed in texture when new. After washing, the cotton fibers will naturally tighten, and the fabric will develop a denser, firmer hand. This change is part of the character of an unwashed cotton jersey garment and helps the material settle into a more substantial and stable feel over time.

Shrinkage and Care
When washed in cold water and line dried in the shade, shrinkage is expected to be relatively moderate. Any shrinkage will generally appear more noticeably in the body length than in the chest width, while the width is expected to remain comparatively stable. Please avoid hot-water washing and tumble drying, as high heat can cause stronger and less predictable shrinkage. For best results, we recommend washing gently in cold water and drying naturally in the shade.

Ringer T-Shirt Details
This item is designed in the style of a classic ringer T-shirt, featuring contrast rib-knit trim at both the neckline and the sleeve openings. The contrast neckband and sleeve trim give the shirt its traditional ringer T-shirt appearance, while also adding visual definition to the overall design. These details are inspired by vintage athletic and casual T-shirts, giving the garment a familiar classic look with a clean, wearable finish.

Collar and Neckline Construction
The collar is built with a contrast rib-knit neckband forming a classic ribbed crew neckline. The rib-knit neckband is attached to the tubular body with a clean, secure seam and finished with single-needle stitching. Inside the neckline, the T-shirt is reinforced with interior neck tape that runs from shoulder to shoulder across the back of the neck. This tape acts as a stabilizer for the neckline seam, helping to reduce distortion from repeated wear and laundering, improving shape retention, and enhancing long-term durability at a high-stress area. Together, the contrast rib-knit neckband, the internal shoulder-to-shoulder taping, and the clean single-needle finish create a collar that stays neat and comfortable.

Sleeve Openings Construction
The sleeve openings are finished with contrast rib-knit trim, a separate rib-knit component that cleanly frames the sleeve edge while adding controlled stretch and recovery. The inner raw edge of the rib-knit trim is finished with overlock stitching to control fraying and maintain a clean interior finish. The rib trim is securely attached to the sleeve opening, while the outer edge is finished with single-needle stitching for a neat and stable appearance. The contrast color also highlights the ringer-style design.

Hem Construction
The hem is constructed with a folded, turned-up hem allowance. The inner raw edge is finished with overlock stitching to control fraying and keep the interior edge clean, while the folded hem is secured from the outside with single-needle stitching. This combination provides a neat interior finish, stable hem construction, and a clean, streamlined appearance that complements the vintage-inspired character of the shirt.

Stitching and Construction
The shoulder seams and armholes are reinforced with double-needle stitching for added durability. These areas receive regular stress during wear, so the use of reinforced stitching helps the garment maintain its structure and withstand daily use. The combination of tubular body construction, reinforced seam work, carefully applied rib-knit trim, internal neck taping, and clean single-needle finishing reflects TOYS McCOY's attention to both vintage-inspired detailing and practical wearability.

Closure
Pull-over style with no front opening or closure. The T-shirt is designed to be worn over the head, preserving the clean, uninterrupted appearance of a classic short-sleeve jersey T-shirt.

Pattern
Graphic print. The front and back are decorated with commemorative TOYS McCOY 30th Anniversary graphic artwork created by the brand. The print is designed to evoke a vintage aesthetic, giving the design an intentionally aged, time-worn appearance.

Graphic Print
The graphics are rendered with a vintage-style distressed print effect, giving them a naturally worn-in appearance similar to an aged vintage T-shirt. This slightly faded and broken-in print character prevents the graphics from looking overly new or flat, adding depth and nostalgic character to the overall design.

30th Anniversary Artwork
The original TOYS McCOY 30th Anniversary graphics are printed on a vintage-inspired tubular body, creating a special commemorative design that highlights the brand's long-standing attention to classic American casualwear and vintage garment construction. The combination of anniversary artwork, textured cotton jersey, contrast ringer trim, and compact silhouette gives this T-shirt a distinctive presence while keeping it easy to wear as part of a modern casual wardrobe.

Sleeve Style
Set-in sleeves. The sleeves are constructed separately and sewn into the armholes, creating a familiar, structured T-shirt silhouette with a clean shoulder line and natural ease of movement.

Sleeve Length
Short sleeves. The sleeve length is designed for everyday casual wear and pairs naturally with the compact body balance of the shirt.

Please Note
The graphic print has been intentionally finished to create a vintage effect. Variations in tone, subtle fading, slight shading, and natural irregularities in the aged appearance are intentional and contribute to the garment's authentic, worn-in look. Please understand that these details are part of the overall aesthetic of the T-shirt and should not be considered defects.

Fit and Sizing
This item is labeled in Japanese sizing and has a compact fit even by Japanese sizing standards, with a trim silhouette and a relatively shorter body length than many standard T-shirts. It may feel smaller than typical U.S. and European sizing. Because fit can vary depending on body type, preferred silhouette, and the design of the garment, please use the actual garment measurements as the main reference and compare them with a similar T-shirt you already own. Since the measurements are taken by hand with a measuring tape, please allow for slight variations due to individual garment differences and the measuring method.

Care Instructions and Technical Explanation (Garment Label Details)

Hand Wash Only
Hand washing is recommended to reduce mechanical stress on the fabric, seams, and printed graphics. This gentle method helps maintain the natural hand feel of the cotton and prevents unnecessary abrasion that may occur during machine washing.

Do Not Bleach
Bleaching agents can damage cotton fibers and cause discoloration, particularly on dyed fabrics and printed areas. Avoiding bleach helps preserve the original color tone and overall fabric strength.

Cool Iron (Use a Pressing Cloth)
If ironing is necessary, use a low-temperature (cool) iron setting and always place a pressing cloth between the iron and the garment. This prevents direct heat contact, protecting the fabric surface, printed graphics, and stitching from heat damage, shine, or scorching. Ironing from the reverse side is also recommended for added protection.

Do Not Dry Clean
Dry cleaning solvents are not suitable for this garment, as they may negatively affect the cotton fibers, print quality, and sewn construction. Wet care methods are preferred to maintain authenticity and material integrity.

Dry in Shade
Air drying in the shade helps prevent color fading and fabric deterioration caused by prolonged exposure to direct sunlight. This is especially important for garments with vintage-inspired dyes and graphics.

In thirteen years of doing this, we have never handled a fabric quite like this one. Faux suede has its roots in Japan, where mills worked out how to split polyester into filaments finer than silk and brush them up into a nap that reads like leather at a glance. The fabric on this coverall comes out of that lineage and then goes somewhere stranger. It looks like suede and behaves like a technical cloth, carrying a stiffness much closer to raw denim, so the jacket stands away from the body and holds its own lines rather than falling soft against you. That structure is the whole point here. It also shrugs off water and asks for none of the careful handling real suede demands, which makes it a jacket you can actually wear in weather. orSlow builds it on its coverall pattern with an A-line silhouette that widens as it falls, and the brand's own buttons and sleeve design handle the details that make it recognizable from across a room. Four rounded pockets break up the front, three of them patch pockets and one a flap pocket, with brass snaps running up the placket and an internal locker loop at the neck. It works across three seasons and settles in nicely the longer you wear it.

Waffle knits earn their place in cold weather through geometry. The honeycomb structure raises and recesses the surface into hundreds of small pockets, and each one holds a little air against the body, which is why waffle insulates while still breathing freely and why it spent a century as the standard for thermal underwear before anyone wore it on the outside. orSlow knits this one in Japan at 5.8oz with a soft hand and a good amount of give, helped along by the single percent of polyurethane blended into the cotton body, which lets the knit stretch as you move and return to shape afterward. The texture is the point as much as the warmth here, breaking up the surface of an outfit in a way a flat jersey leaves alone. Ribbing finishes the collar and the sleeve ends in 100% cotton. One thing worth knowing before the first wash: the fabric is not pre-rinsed, so orSlow expects roughly 3 to 4% shrinkage, which works out to about half an inch to an inch across most dimensions and a little more through the length.

product.title: 11oz - Work Shirt Roll-Dyed Selvedge Canvas - Dark Brown
product.body_html:
Dye behaves differently depending on when it meets the cloth. Rogue Territory sends this 11oz Japanese selvedge canvas through a roll dye in its raw state, which lays the brown onto the surface of the yarns rather than driving it all the way to the core. That is the same principle behind a good pair of raw jeans, and it sets the shirt up to shed pigment slowly, lightening at the elbows, the cuffs, the placket, and anywhere else the fabric moves against itself. The dyeing happens in Los Angeles, a short trip from the floor where the shirts are sewn. Once construction is finished, each piece goes through an industrial wash that pulls some of the surface dye back off, so the shirt arrives with a worn-in patina already started and a hand that has lost its stiffness. The wash also means the brown stays where it belongs, so you can wear it over anything. Inside, contrast red chain stitching runs the seams and ties back to the bold red selvedge ID, and the placket is cut on the selvedge so that finished edge faces out every time the shirt is open. The canvas carries a natural stretch that lets it relax into shape quickly. Dual chest pockets, triple-needle chainstitched seams with run-off, a herringbone locker loop, and antiqued brass snaps handle the rest.

product.body_html:
Shadow plaid earns its name by hiding in plain sight. product.title: 13oz - Foxfibre® Green Weft Selvedge - True Guy
product.body_html:
Iron is the quiet trick behind this fabric. Green FoxFibre® comes off the plant already carrying color, and treating it with iron, a mineral mordant that natural dyers have leaned on for centuries, sets off a reaction with the pigment already sitting inside the fiber rather than laying new color over the top of it. What comes out the other side is a deeper, steadier green-grey, and because the color lives in the fiber instead of coating it, washing and wear push the tone further along rather than stripping it away. Naked & Famous runs that weft against indigo rope-dyed warp yarns in a 13oz Japanese selvedge, which sets up the long game: as the indigo gives way at the knees and the seat, the green-grey underneath comes forward. Green is the difficult one in the FoxFibre® family. Sally Fox began selectively breeding naturally pigmented cotton in the 1980s to take chemical dyeing out of the equation, and the green variety she developed grows shorter fibers at much lower yields than the brown, which makes it harder to spin consistently and keeps the supply thin. For this denim the cotton is grown in the United States and the yarn is spun in Osaka, putting American organic agriculture and Japanese weaving on the same loom. A 5oz natural vegetable-tanned leather patch sits at the waistband, ready to darken and take on its own patina alongside the denim, with tin hardware and a button fly closing things out.
